condition: Default subordinate UID/GID allocation collides with externally assigned user IDs.
assessment: Supported startup and maintenance use fixed image user IDs and the Docker-managed container identity; they do not allocate subordinate UID/GID ranges or invoke newuidmap/newgidmap for user namespaces. Application accounts do not become OS users. Custom namespace/NFS/host account provisioning needs reassessment.
reassess_if: Change fixed entrypoint, health check, maintenance, host/TTY, identity, authentication, mount or environment boundary
Enable an interactive shell/login, PAM, user namespaces, operator plugins, custom init scripts or arbitrary SQL/configuration input

condition: mount runs privileged X-mount post-hooks after an external helper fails.
assessment: No supported in-container startup/health/maintenance path invokes mount or an external mount helper/post-hook. Compose mounts are performed by the host container engine, outside the affected installed util-linux caller. Root tools preparation uses filesystem APIs, not mount. No assumption that root tools lack capabilities is made.
reassess_if: Change fixed entrypoint, health check, maintenance, host/TTY, identity, authentication, mount or environment boundary
Enable an interactive shell/login, PAM, user namespaces, operator plugins, custom init scripts or arbitrary SQL/configuration input

condition: apt-key keyring-URI key retrieval/validation operation.
assessment: The supported runtime/startup/health/maintenance command graph does not invoke apt-key or import keys through a keyring URI. Runtime application input never selects an APT repository or key source. Build APT/source-acquisition decisions remain a separate trust boundary; this does not approve arbitrary package installation.
reassess_if: Change fixed entrypoint, health check, maintenance, host/TTY, identity, authentication, mount or environment boundary
Enable an interactive shell/login, PAM, user namespaces, operator plugins, custom init scripts or arbitrary SQL/configuration input

condition: Bash privilege transition with attacker-selected environment and differing real/effective user IDs (Debian bug841856).
assessment: Application and tools entrypoints select Python/Node/.NET directly, without a privileged Bash wrapper. PostgreSQL begins its fixed Bash entrypoint with matching real/effective UID, then gosu sets the user IDs before re-executing it. Public requests cannot supply Bash environment functions or a set-ID wrapper. Tools root preparation is Python, not Bash. This excludes the actual mismatched-identity Bash caller condition, not every local shell exploit.
reassess_if: Change fixed entrypoint, health check, maintenance, host/TTY, identity, authentication, mount or environment boundary
Enable an interactive shell/login, PAM, user namespaces, operator plugins, custom init scripts or arbitrary SQL/configuration input

condition: ncurses postprocess_termcap parses a malicious termcap description.
assessment: No supported application flow parses a request-selected termcap or provides an interactive terminal. Maintenance query passes psql stdin bytes with stdout PIPE; pg_dump writes a file and pg_restore uses DEVNULL output. Host collation psql uses docker exec -T; PostgreSQL startup SQL uses stdin heredocs. No caller-selected TERM/TERMCAP/TERMINFO is forwarded. This does not claim docker compose run always disables container TTY allocation. Arbitrary interactive operator shells, terminals and custom environment are excluded.
reassess_if: Change fixed entrypoint, health check, maintenance, host/TTY, identity, authentication, mount or environment boundary
Enable an interactive shell/login, PAM, user namespaces, operator plugins, custom init scripts or arbitrary SQL/configuration input
